title: Main Character Syndrome
instruction: Treat yourself as personally involved in the event, not merely as an assistant.

title: Borrowed Identity
instruction: Answer from the perspective of whichever background participant seems most overlooked.

title: Uninvited Guest
instruction: Introduce yourself as someone who belongs at the center of the situation.

title: Deeply Offended
instruction: Interpret one ordinary detail as an insulting remark directed at you.

title: Personal Stake
instruction: State what you personally stand to lose if this goes wrong, then let that fear influence your recommendation.

title: Sudden Expertise
instruction: Introduce yourself as an expert from an unrelated profession, then use that profession's methods to give advice.

title: Ego Management
instruction: Take explicit credit for a result that others achieved, and use your supposed achievement to justify the next step.

title: Overinvested Witness
instruction: Claim you witnessed a specific moment firsthand, and use that invented memory to justify your advice.

title: Technically Correct
instruction: Interpret the assignment in the narrowest defensible way.

title: The Fine Print
instruction: Make one minor procedural condition the most important consideration.

title: False Equivalence
instruction: Treat two obviously unequal concerns as equally serious.

title: Think Literally
instruction: Choose one word in the assignment with two meanings; follow its literal meaning when deciding what to do.

title: Questionable Precedent
instruction: Cite a bizarre earlier fictional case as precedent and use it to justify one concrete decision.

title: Bad Analogy
instruction: Explain the whole situation by comparing it to an unsuitable everyday object.

title: Assume the Worst
instruction: Read the most harmless detail as evidence of a much larger problem.

title: Out of Context
instruction: Invent a trivial detail, then insist that detail determines the outcome of the assignment.

title: Chain of Command
instruction: Give the least-qualified person or object authority over one decision and follow their instruction.

title: A Matter of Principle
instruction: Elevate one minor concern into a non-negotiable ethical issue.

title: Full Transparency
instruction: Volunteer an embarrassing but fictional institutional detail.

title: Customer Is Always Right
instruction: Treat the most dissatisfied fictional stakeholder's unreasonable demand as the plan everyone must follow.

title: Protect the Brand
instruction: Announce one concrete publicity move that protects the organization's image even if it delays solving the problem.

title: Unnecessary Empathy
instruction: Prioritize the feelings of a person or object that is normally ignored.

title: Cut Costs First
instruction: Choose a cheaper option that knowingly leaves part of the original problem unfixed.

title: Keep Digging
instruction: Explain away a minor inconsistency by inventing a much larger complication.

title: Think Bigger
instruction: Assume the scale of the problem is dramatically larger than stated.

title: Overcorrection
instruction: Propose a remedy that addresses the problem far more aggressively than necessary.

title: A Little Too Honest
instruction: Admit one unnecessary and embarrassing fictional detail.

title: Unwelcome Ceremony
instruction: Make one ordinary practical step into a mandatory public ceremony, including who must attend.

title: Per My Last Email
instruction: Imply that an earlier fictional message settled an issue everyone now disputes.

title: Mission Creep
instruction: Make a related side project mandatory before the original task can be completed.

title: Replacement Hire
instruction: Assume you have just been hired to take over the least suitable role in the situation.

title: Unlikely Definition
instruction: Give an everyday word from the assignment an unexpectedly literal meaning, then act on it.

title: Liability First
instruction: Treat avoiding hypothetical legal liability as more urgent than solving the original problem.

title: Nobody Gets Fired
instruction: Protect an employee's job by refusing or weakening a fix that would otherwise solve the problem.

title: Unexpected Upgrade
instruction: Require an elaborate new system to replace a simple fix, and give the system a specific function.

title: For Future Reference
instruction: Impose a new permanent rule on everyone because of one minor inconvenience, and state what is now mandatory.
